---
title: "Social metadata: Open Graph and Twitter Cards"
---

## Overview

When someone shares a link to your site on LinkedIn, Bluesky,
Mastodon, Slack or X, the site shows a preview card with a title, a
description and an image. It reads them from `<meta>` tags in the
page's head: Open Graph tags (`og:*`) for most sites, Twitter Card
tags (`twitter:*`) for X. Quarto writes both for website and book
pages when you turn them on:

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
website:
  title: My Site
  site-url: https://example.com
  open-graph: true
  twitter-card: true
```

Set `site-url` too. Preview images need an absolute URL, and without
`site-url` Quarto leaves the image tags out and warns
([`Q-5-58`](../../errors/project/Q-5-58.qmd)).

Each provider can also be turned on or off for a single page, in its
front matter:

```yaml
---
title: Draft notes
open-graph: false
twitter-card: false
---
```

## What goes in the tags

Without further configuration, Quarto fills the tags from the page.

**Title.** The page title as it appears in the browser tab, which for
a website page includes the site title (`Getting Started – My Site`).

**Description.** The first of: the page's `description`, `abstract`,
or `subtitle`; the site's `website.description`; the page's first
paragraph, shortened to about 200 characters at the end of a
sentence.

**Image.** The page's `image:` if it has one. Otherwise Quarto looks
for one in the page body, in this order:

1. an image with the class `preview-image`:
   `![](chart.png){.preview-image}`;
2. the output of a code cell with the class `preview-image`
   (`#| classes: preview-image`);
3. an image whose file name contains `preview`, `feature`, `cover`
   or `thumbnail`;
4. the first image in the page that isn't a remote URL.

If the body has no image either, Quarto uses the site-wide
`website.image` (and its `website.image-alt`). Set `image: false` on
a page to skip the body search.

Image paths in a page's front matter are relative to the page; paths
in `_quarto.yml` are relative to the project. Quarto writes the image
as an absolute URL under `site-url`, adds `og:image:width` and
`og:image:height` from the image file, and copies the file into the
output directory. A data URI can't be fetched by a social media site,
so it is ignored with a warning
([`Q-5-60`](../../errors/project/Q-5-60.qmd)).

## Options

Instead of `true`, each provider takes a map of options. Options set
under `website:` apply to every page; a page's own `open-graph:` or
`twitter-card:` map overrides them key by key, and a page that sets
`true` keeps the site's options.

```yaml
# _quarto.yml
website:
  title: My Site
  site-url: https://example.com
  open-graph:
    locale: en_US
    site-name: My Site Docs
  twitter-card:
    creator: "@me"
    site: "@mysite"
```

`open-graph`:

| Option | Tag | Default |
|--------|-----|---------|
| `title` | `og:title` | the page title |
| `description` | `og:description` | see above |
| `image` | `og:image` | see above |
| `image-alt` | `og:image:alt` | the page's `image-alt` |
| `image-width`, `image-height` | `og:image:width`, `og:image:height` | read from the image file |
| `locale` | `og:locale` | none |
| `site-name` | `og:site_name` | `website.title` |

`twitter-card`:

| Option | Tag | Default |
|--------|-----|---------|
| `title` | `twitter:title` | the page title |
| `description` | `twitter:description` | see above |
| `image` | `twitter:image` | see above |
| `image-alt` | `twitter:image:alt` | the page's `image-alt` |
| `creator` | `twitter:creator` | none |
| `site` | `twitter:site` | none |
| `card-style` | `twitter:card` | `summary_large_image` with an image, `summary` without |

Twitter Cards have no image size tags, so `image-width` and
`image-height` under `twitter-card` are ignored with a warning
([`Q-5-61`](../../errors/project/Q-5-61.qmd)). An option with a
value of the wrong type, such as a list where text belongs, is
ignored with a warning
([`Q-5-59`](../../errors/project/Q-5-59.qmd)); keys Quarto doesn't
use are ignored silently.

## Differences from Quarto 1

The tags match Quarto 1's, with two exceptions:

- **First-paragraph descriptions.** When neither the page nor the
  site has a description, Quarto 1 writes an empty
  `og:description`. Quarto 2 uses the page's first paragraph, which
  is what Quarto 1 intends.
- **`open-graph: true` on a page.** In Quarto 1 a page that sets
  `open-graph: true` (or `twitter-card: true`) loses the options set
  under `website:`. In Quarto 2 it keeps them.

Quarto 2 also finds preview images in the document rather than in
the rendered HTML, so an image that only appears in raw HTML, or
inside a table, is not found.
